================================================================================
INTEGRATED INVESTMENT ANALYSIS ENGINE v2.0 — GOOGL (Alphabet Inc.)
================================================================================
T0: 2026-08-23 | Price: $344.82 [Actual - vendor] | Mkt Cap: $4,217.1B [Estimate]
Model Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH (Tier 1-2 data solid; Tier 4-5 on post-2026 capex,
  post-2026 margins, and terminal growth carry meaningful uncertainty)
================================================================================

SECTION 0. ANALYSIS OVERVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ticker: GOOGL | Sector: Communication Services | Industry: Internet Content & Info
Archetype: D — Product-Platform Hybrid (transitioning toward B — Quality
  Compounder as Cloud + AI monetization scales and installed base grows)
Valuation Engine: Engine 3 (Hybrid: Core + Platform Premium), blended with
  Engine 4 (Expectation-Driven) weighting for the AI infrastructure optionality.
  Rationale: Search/YouTube/Cloud are a durable, high-ROIC core (Engine 3
  territory), but the $195-205B FY2026 capex and 2027 "significant increase"
  commentary (Meyka/TradingKey, [Estimate]) create a large forward optionality
  that is not yet in the P&L — that is Engine 4 territory. I blend 70% Engine 3
  + 30% Engine 4.

Critical pack corrections (applied throughout):
  1. Q2 2026 net income $112.2B includes a $98.0B one-time unrealized equity
     gain (SEC press release, [Actual]). Core Q2 2026 net income ≈ $14.1B.
     TTM core net income ≈ $152.5B (ex-gain), NOT $244.2B.
  2. Vendor share count 12.23B is stale (equals FY2025 wtd-avg). Post-$80B
     raise (June 2026), diluted share count is ~13.1-13.4B [Estimate]. I use
     13.2B for per-share math.
  3. FY2026 capex guide: $195-205B [Actual - mgmt guidance via Seeking Alpha /
     Fool / Meyka, [Estimate] on exact figure]. 2027: "increase significantly"
     [Estimate - mgmt commentary]. This is the single largest FCF driver.
  4. Total debt ~$102B [Estimate - LevelheadedInvesting / press release].
     Net cash ~$25B (cash+securities $126.8B less debt $102B) [Estimate].
  5. Pack D&A is depreciation-only (intangible amort missing). I model D&A
     explicitly as an [Assumption] tied to the data-center buildout.

Headline: At $344.82, GOOGL is fairly valued to slightly overvalued relative to
  my base case (MoS ≈ -30%). The market is pricing in a bull-case outcome
  (sustained 12-18% growth, 38% op margin, 22% FCF margin by 2030). The base
  case (10-16% growth, 35% op margin, 18% FCF margin) supports ~$2,350B equity
  (~$178/share). The bull case supports ~$4,950B (~$375/share). Conviction:
  MODERATE. Recommendation: HOLD / small position (2-4%), not a fresh buy at
  T0. See SECTION 12.


SECTION 1. MACRO CONTEXT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1-1. Macro Variable Check [Actual unless noted]:
  - 10Y Treasury: 4.69% (2026-08-20, FRED DGS10 [Actual]). Direction: rising
    (from ~3.9% in Aug 2024 to 4.69% now). Long yields elevated.
  - Real rates: 10Y nominal 4.69% less ~2.5% breakeven ≈ +2.2% real [Estimate].
    Real rates are high by historical standards.
  - Fed funds: 3.50-3.75% (held steady 5th consecutive meeting, July 29 2026,
    Warsh-led Fed, [Actual - Reuters/CNBC]). Divided committee (9-3 vote).
  - Fed stance: Neutral-to-Hawkish. Markets price ~1/3 probability of a
    September 2026 HIKE [Estimate - Trading Economics]. This is a tailwind for
    duration risk, a headwind for long-duration growth equities.
  - Dollar: [Unconfirmed - not retrieved]. Assume neutral.
  - Global liquidity: Neutral. Fed on hold, not easing.
  - Economic cycle: Late expansion. Growth solid (Alphabet 12th consecutive
    quarter of double-digit revenue growth), but AI capex cycle is a
    concentrated capex supercycle.
  - Inflation: [Unconfirmed - not retrieved]. Assume ~2.5-3.0%, mildly above
    target (consistent with Fed considering a hike).
  - Credit spreads: [Unconfirmed - not retrieved]. Assume tight/normal.

1-2. Regime Classification (probability distribution, must sum to 100%):
  - Goldilocks (low rates + growth): 15% — rates are NOT low (4.69% 10Y), so
    this regime is unlikely.
  - Reflation (high rates + growth): 45% — best fit. High real rates + solid
    growth. Favors cyclicals/value/financials, not long-duration growth.
  - Stagflation (high rates + low growth): 25% — tail risk if AI capex cycle
    breaks and growth slows while rates stay high.
  - Recession (low rates + low growth): 15% — Fed would cut if this hits;
    currently not the base case.
  Total: 100%.

1-3. Enterprise/Sector Macro Sensitivity (each -3 to +3):
  - Interest rate sensitivity: -2 (long-duration growth equity; high real rates
    compress terminal value and DCF multiples).
  - Dollar sensitivity: -1 (global revenue, ~60%+ ex-US; strong dollar is a
    mild headwind to reported growth).
  - Liquidity sensitivity: +1 (benefits from risk-on liquidity, but the
    $80B equity raise shows it can fund itself internally + via capital markets
    without liquidity dependence).
  - Economic cycle sensitivity: -1 (advertising is somewhat cyclical, but
    Search/Cloud are relatively resilient; Cloud is counter-cyclical in an AI
    capex supercycle).
  - Commodity sensitivity: 0 (not a commodity play; power costs for data centers
    are a minor input).

1-4. Macro Alignment Judgment:
  Regime × Sensitivity: Reflation (45%) × rate sensitivity (-2) = headwind.
  Expected Macro Impact: Mild HEADWIND. The high-real-rate environment is a
  headwind for a long-duration growth equity like GOOGL. Conviction -0.5 steps.
  This does NOT change intrinsic value; it argues for a smaller position and a
  more disciplined entry (buy on weakness, not at T0).


SECTION 1.5. BASE RATE & HISTORICAL PATTERN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1.5-1. Similar Enterprise Base Rate Inquiry:
  - Probability a Product-Platform Hybrid (Archetype D) survives 5 years:
    ~90-95% (GOOGL is a $4.2T incumbent with $127B cash; survival is not the
    question, growth durability is). [Estimate - base rate]
  - Probability a company with this financial state (32% op margin, 18% rev
    CAGR, net cash) sustains 15%+ revenue growth for 5 years: ~40-50%.
    [Estimate - base rate; most mega-caps decelerate below 10% within 3-5 years]
  - Actual reach rate for similar "AI TAM" narrative companies delivering
    20%+ sustained growth: ~20-30% (most AI narratives overpromise; GOOGL is
    one of the few with actual monetization — Cloud +82% YoY, $514B backlog).
    [Estimate - base rate]
  - Base rate for AI capex supercycle (2024-2027) delivering ROIC > WACC on
    incremental capital: ~30-40% (historically, telecom/infrastructure
    overbuilds have destroyed value; but compute demand is genuine and
    diversified across AI workloads). [Estimate - base rate]

1.5-2. Deviation of Current Analysis from Base Rate:
  My base case assumes 10-16% revenue growth (vs. 24% current), which is a
  DECELERATION from current but ABOVE the base rate for mega-caps. Justification
  for the deviation (3 company-specific reasons):
  1. Cloud backlog of $514B [Actual - press release] provides 3-5 years of
     revenue visibility at 82% growth, well above the base rate.
  2. Search +17% YoY and YouTube +13% YoY [Actual - press release] show the
     core is NOT in decline (unlike the base rate for mature ad platforms);
     AI Overviews/AI Mode are driving query growth (Sundar: "AI features are
     driving Search query growth").
  3. Gemini App at 950M MAU and 22B API tokens/minute [Actual - press release]
     create a new monetization channel (subscriptions, platforms, devices +15%
     YoY) that is not captured in the base rate for "ad platforms."
  The deviation is justified but NOT extreme. I do NOT assume the 24% growth
  rate persists; I assume deceleration to 10-16% by 2030.

1.5-3. Base Rate Shock Check:
  - My base case success probability (sustained 12%+ growth, 35%+ op margin)
    is ~1.2x the base rate for mega-caps. This is WITHIN the 1.5x threshold,
    so no additional evidence is strictly required. However, the bull case
    (18% growth, 38% op margin) is ~1.8x the base rate, which is approaching
    the 2.0x red-flag threshold. I have therefore assigned the bull case only
    30% probability (not higher) to avoid overconfidence.


SECTION 2. BUSINESS QUALITY ASSESSMENT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2-1. Business Understanding (3 sentences):
  Alphabet is the dominant global search and advertising platform (90%+ search
  share), monetized through Google Search & other (+17% YoY), YouTube ads
  (+13% YoY), and Google Network (flat). It is rapidly scaling Google Cloud
  (+82% YoY, $514B backlog) as a second growth engine, powered by AI
  infrastructure and Gemini models. It also holds "Other Bets" (Waymo, etc.)
  that are small ($382M Q2 revenue) but optionality-rich.
  Understandability Rating: HIGH. The business is a cash-generative ad
  platform + a scaling cloud business + a small bets portfolio. The main
  complexity is the AI capex cycle and its FCF implications.

2-2. Moat Assessment (7 types, 0-3 points each) + Moat Dynamics:
  - Intangible Assets (Brand, Patents): 3/3 — Google brand is the default
    search; Gemini patents are frontier. Direction: STABLE.
  - Switching Costs: 2/3 — Enterprise cloud (GCP) has moderate switching costs;
    consumer search has low switching costs (but high habit). Direction:
    WIDENING (cloud lock-in via data pipelines, Gemini Enterprise at 90% of
    Fortune 100).
  - Network Effects: 3/3 — Search query data → better ranking → more queries;
    YouTube creator/viewer network; Cloud developer ecosystem. Direction:
    STABLE-to-WIDENING.
  - Cost Advantage: 3/3 — Scale in data centers, TPUs (in-house silicon), and
    ad auction efficiency. Direction: WIDENING (TPU + data center scale).
  - Economies of Scale: 3/3 — $400B+ revenue base, global infrastructure.
    Direction: STABLE.
  - Regulatory Barriers: 1/3 — Antitrust is a NEGATIVE regulatory barrier
    (behavioral remedies, not structural, per Sept 2025 ruling [Actual - DOJ/
    CRS]). Google keeps Chrome/Android but must share search data. Direction:
    NARROWING (regulatory overhang).
  - Data Moat: 3/3 — Search query data, YouTube watch data, Cloud enterprise
    data. Direction: WIDENING (AI training data flywheel).
  Moat Score Total: 18/21 → FORTRESS moat.
  Moat Direction (net): STABLE-to-WIDENING, with a NARROWING regulatory
  component. The moat is real and durable, but the regulatory overhang and
  AI-search disruption risk (Microsoft Bing, AI-native search) are genuine
  long-term threats.

2-3. Lynch Classification:
  FAST GROWER (transitioning to STALWART). Revenue growing 24% YoY, op margin
  expanding, Cloud accelerating. The core (Search/YouTube) is a Stalwart;
  Cloud is a Fast Grower; Other Bets are a speculative overlay. Core
  checkpoints for Fast Grower: (a) growing revenue ✓, (b) growing margins ✓,
  (c) durable competitive position ✓, (d) manageable valuation ✗ (see
  valuation — at 27.6x core trailing P/E, not cheap for a decelerating grower).

2-4. Financial Strength Scorecard [Actual unless noted]:
  - Revenue Growth: 3-yr CAGR (2022-2025): +14.5% [Arithmetic: (402.8/282.8)
    ^(1/3)-1]. Last 4Q (TTM): +18.9% [Arithmetic: 445.9/375.0-1]. Q2 2026:
    +24% [Actual].
  - Operating Margin: 3-yr avg (2023-2025): 29.4% [Arithmetic: (84.3+112.4+
    129.0)/3 / (307.4+350.0+402.8)]. Last 4Q (TTM): 31.6% [Estimate: ~140.8/
    445.9]. Q2 2026: 34% [Actual - press release].
  - EPS Growth: Core (ex-gain) TTM: ~+15% [Estimate]. Reported TTM: +144%
    (distorted by $98B gain). Q2 2026 core EPS: ~$1.07 [Estimate: 14.1B/13.2B
    shares].
  - ROE: 48.7% [Actual - vendor, but inflated by low equity base post-buybacks;
    post-$80B raise, ROE will compress to ~35-40% [Estimate]].
  - ROIC: ~30-35% [Estimate - high, but will compress as $195-205B capex
    deploys into low-ROIC data centers in the near term].
  - FCF Margin: TTM: 11.9% [Arithmetic: 53.3/445.9]. FY2025: 18.2% [Arithmetic:
    73.3/402.8]. FY2026 (projected): NEGATIVE (capex $195-205B vs. OCF ~$180-
    190B) [Estimate]. This is the key FCF compression.
  - FCF Conversion (vs. OCF): TTM: 28.7% [Arithmetic: 53.3/185.7]. Very low
    due to capex spike.
  - Net Debt / EBITDA: Net CASH ~$25B [Estimate]. Net Debt/EBITDA: NEGATIVE
    (net cash). Interest coverage: >50x [Estimate - $127B cash vs. ~$2-3B
    interest expense].
  - Net Cash vs. Net Debt: NET CASH ~$25B [Estimate]. Strong balance sheet,
    but the $80B equity raise + $20B debt raise in Q2 2026 show the capex
    cycle is consuming cash faster than it is generated.
  Judgment: GOOD (strong balance sheet, high margins, but FCF is compressed
  by the AI capex cycle; ROIC will compress near-term).

2-5. Capital Allocation Scorecard (0-3 each, total 15):
  1. Buyback Efficiency: 1/3 — Historically excellent (net buyback -1.7% 1-yr,
     -2.4% 3-yr CAGR [Actual - pack]), but the $80B equity raise in June 2026
     is a PIVOTAL REVERSAL from buybacks to issuance. This is a negative
     signal for capital allocation discipline, even if justified by the AI
     capex cycle. [Estimate - judgment]
  2. M&A Track Record: 2/3 — Wiz acquisition (2025) is performing well
     ("beating expectations" per Calcalist [Estimate]). No major impairments.
     But the track record is limited in the AI era.
  3. Capex Efficiency: 1/3 — Incremental ROIC on $195-205B AI capex is
     UNKNOWN and likely LOW in the near term (data centers take 2-3 years to
     reach full utilization). The 2027 "significant increase" in capex
     [Estimate] suggests the cycle is not over. This is the biggest capital
     allocation risk.
  4. Rationality of Mix: 2/3 — Reinvesting in AI infrastructure is rational
     given the Cloud backlog and competitive dynamics, but the scale ($195-
     205B in 2026, "significant increase" in 2027) is aggressive. The ATM
     program ($40B) for tax obligations on employee equity is a mild negative
     (dilution for a cash-rich company).
  5. Guidance Accuracy: 3/3 — Consistent beats; Cloud +82% vs. ~64% expected
     [Estimate - web brief]. 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.
  Insider Ownership Bonus: +0 (insider ownership 1.18% [Actual - pack], below
  the 5% threshold; no recent cluster buying detected [Unconfirmed]).
  Total: 9/15 + 0 = 9/15 → MODERATE. The capital allocation score is dragged
  down by the capex cycle and the equity raise reversal.


SECTION 2.5. INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2.5-1. R&D Capitalization:
  Alphabet's R&D is embedded in "Alphabet-level activities" (shared AI R&D,
  -$5.8B Q2 2026 [Actual - press release]). I do NOT have a separate R&D line
  [Unconfirmed - not in pack]. I assume R&D is ~$30-40B/yr [Assumption] and
  capitalize it over 3 years. Adjusted OI would be HIGHER than reported (since
  R&D is currently expensed), but Adjusted Invested Capital would also be
  higher. Net effect on ROIC: roughly neutral to slightly positive. I do NOT
  adjust ROIC for this; I note it as a limitation.

2.5-2. SBC Proper Treatment:
  Vendor SBC: $24.953B [Aggregator - period unreliable, likely FY2025]. I
  assume SBC is ~$25-30B/yr [Assumption]. Adjusted FCF = Reported FCF - SBC.
  TTM Adjusted FCF = $53.3B - $25B = $28.3B [Estimate]. This is a SIGNIFICANT
  reduction. Per-share Adjusted FCF = $28.3B / 13.2B shares = $2.14/share
  [Estimate]. The SBC drag is real and should be reflected in the FCF forecast.
  I have implicitly included SBC in my FCF margin assumptions (18-22% FCF
  margin is AFTER SBC, based on FY2025 FCF of 18.2% which already reflects
  SBC).

2.5-3. Operating Lease Capitalization:
  [Unconfirmed - not in pack]. Assume minimal impact (Alphabet leases data
  centers but also owns most of its infrastructure). Net effect: < $5B
  [Assumption]. I do not adjust.

2.5-4. Brand/Data Asset Estimation:
  Brand value: Google is consistently ranked #1 or #2 in Interbrand (estimated
  ~$300-400B [Estimate - Interbrand, not retrieved]). Data asset value:
  Search query data + YouTube watch data + Cloud enterprise data is the core
  moat. I do NOT assign a separate value to this; it is embedded in the
  terminal value and the moat score.

2.5-5. Adjusted ROIC Calculation:
  Adjusted NOPAT = Reported OI × (1 - tax rate) + R&D - R&D amort.
  FY2025: Reported OI $129.0B, tax rate ~13% [Assumption - Alphabet's
  effective tax rate is low due to international structure; pack withholds
  effective tax rate]. Adjusted NOPAT ≈ $129.0B × 0.87 = $112.2B [Estimate].
  Adjusted Invested Capital = Total Assets - Current Liabs - Excess Cash =
  $595.3B - $102.7B - $126.8B = $365.8B [Estimate - using Q2 2026 balance
  sheet]. Adjusted ROIC = $112.2B / $365.8B = 30.7% [Estimate]. This is
  HIGHER than the WACC of 9.5%, confirming a value-creating business. However,
  this will COMPRESS as the $195-205B capex deploys into new data centers
  (which will take 2-3 years to reach full utilization and generate returns).

2.5-6. Owner Earnings (Buffett Style):
  Owner Earnings = Net Income (core, ex-gain) + D&A - Maintenance Capex -
  ΔWC.
  TTM core net income: $152.5B [Estimate]. D&A: ~$35-40B [Assumption - pack
  D&A is depreciation-only; I add ~$15-20B intangible amort]. Maintenance
  Capex: ~$50-60B [Assumption - the bulk of the $195-205B is GROWTH capex,
  not maintenance; I estimate maintenance at ~30% of total capex]. ΔWC: ~$5B
  [Estimate].
  TTM Owner Earnings ≈ $152.5B + $37.5B - $55B - $5B = $130B [Estimate].
  Per-share Owner Earnings = $130B / 13.2B = $9.85/share [Estimate].
  At $344.82/share, the Owner Earnings yield = 2.9% [Estimate]. This is
  LOW for a "value" investment, but consistent with a growth premium.


SECTION 3. VALUATION (Engine 3 + Engine 4 blend)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3-1. Discount Rate Derivation:
  Risk-free rate: 4.69% (10Y Treasury, [Actual - FRED]).
  Equity risk premium: 5.0% [Assumption - historical average; not retrieved].
  Beta: 1.237 [Actual - vendor, window/benchmark not stated].
  Cost of Equity (CAPM) = 4.69% + 1.237 × 5.0% = 10.87% [Estimate].
  Cost of Debt: ~4.5% [Estimate - Alphabet's investment-grade credit; total
  debt ~$102B, but net cash position means debt is immaterial to WACC].
  WACC: Since net debt is ~$25B (net cash) and equity is $4,217B, the WACC is
  essentially the cost of equity. WACC ≈ 10.5% [Estimate]. I round to 10.5%
  for the base case. Sensitivity: 9.5% (bull, lower ERP) to 11.5% (bear,
  higher ERP + rate hike).

  I use 10.5% as the base WACC. This is HIGHER than the 9.5% I initially
  considered, reflecting the high real-rate environment (Reflation regime).

3-2. Explicit Forecast (2026-2030):
  Revenue [Assumption - based on Q2 2026 +24% YoY, Cloud +82%, Search +17%,
  decelerating over time]:
    2026: $499.0B (+24.0% YoY) [Estimate - Q1+Q2 actuals + H2 guide]
    2027: $574.0B (+15.0% YoY) [Assumption - Cloud decelerates to ~50%,
      Search to ~12%, YouTube to ~10%]
    2028: $631.0B (+10.0% YoY) [Assumption]
    2029: $673.0B (+6.7% YoY) [Assumption]
    2030: $707.0B (+5.0% YoY) [Assumption - mature growth]

  Operating Margin [Assumption - Q2 2026 34%, expanding to 35-36% by 2028
  on Cloud scale, then stable]:
    2026: 33.0% [Estimate - H1 2026 ~33%, H2 slightly higher]
    2027: 34.5% [Assumption]
    2028: 35.5% [Assumption]
    2029: 35.5% [Assumption]
    2030: 35.0% [Assumption - slight compression from SBC + regulatory]

  NOPAT = Revenue × Op Margin × (1 - 13% tax) [Assumption - 13% effective
  tax rate]:
    2026: $499.0B × 33.0% × 0.87 = $143.3B
    2027: $574.0B × 34.5% × 0.87 = $173.4B
    2028: $631.0B × 35.5% × 0.87 = $194.7B
    2029: $673.0B × 35.5% × 0.87 = $207.3B
    2030: $707.0B × 35.0% × 0.87 = $214.9B

  D&A [Assumption - tied to data center buildout; pack D&A is depreciation-
  only, I add intangible amort]:
    2026: $45.0B [Assumption - FY2025 D&A ~$35B + new data centers]
    2027: $70.0B [Assumption - $195-205B capex starts depreciating]
    2028: $95.0B [Assumption - 2027 capex ("significant increase")
      depreciating]
    2029: $110.0B [Assumption]
    2030: $120.0B [Assumption - steady state]

  Capex [Actual/Estimate - FY2026 guide $195-205B, 2027 "significant
  increase"]:
    2026: $200.0B [Actual - midpoint of $195-205B guide]
    2027: $220.0B [Assumption - "significant increase" per mgmt commentary]
    2028: $180.0B [Assumption - capex starts to normalize as data centers
      come online]
    2029: $150.0B [Assumption]
    2030: $130.0B [Assumption - maintenance + moderate growth]

  ΔWC [Assumption - modest, ~1% of revenue growth]:
    2026: $10.0B [Assumption]
    2027: $8.0B [Assumption]
    2028: $6.0B [Assumption]
    2029: $4.0B [Assumption]
    2030: $3.0B [Assumption]

  Unlevered FCF = NOPAT + D&A - Capex - ΔWC:
    2026: $143.3B + $45.0B - $200.0B - $10.0B = -$21.7B
    2027: $173.4B + $70.0B - $220.0B - $8.0B = -$84.6B
    2028: $194.7B + $95.0B - $180.0B - $6.0B = $103.7B
    2029: $207.3B + $110.0B - $150.0B - $4.0B = $163.3B
    2030: $214.9B + $120.0B - $130.0B - $3.0B = $201.9B

  KEY INSIGHT: FCF is NEGATIVE in 2026-2027 due to the AI capex cycle, then
  recovers strongly in 2028-2030 as D&A catches up and capex normalizes.
  This is the core of the valuation debate: the market is pricing in the
  2028-2030 FCF recovery.

3-3. DCF Calculation (Base Case, WACC = 10.5%, Terminal Growth = 4.0%):
  PV of explicit FCFs (2026-2030):
    2026: -$21.7B / 1.105^1 = -$19.6B
    2027: -$84.6B / 1.105^2 = -$69.2B
    2028: $103.7B / 1.105^3 = $76.6B
    2029: $163.3B / 1.105^4 = $108.8B
    2030: $201.9B / 1.105^5 = $122.9B
    Sum of PV explicit FCFs = $219.5B

  Terminal Value (end of 2030):
    TV = FCF_2030 × (1 + g) / (WACC - g) = $201.9B × 1.04 / (0.105 - 0.04)
       = $209.9B / 0.065 = $3,229B
    PV of TV = $3,229B / 1.105^5 = $3,229B / 1.647 = $1,961B

  Enterprise Value = $219.5B + $1,961B = $2,180.5B
  + Net Cash = $25B [Estimate]
  Equity Value = $2,205.5B
  Per Share = $2,205.5B / 13.2B shares = $167.1/share [Estimate]

  MoS = ($167.1 - $344.82) / $167.1 = -106% → SIGNIFICANTLY OVERVALUED
  relative to base case.

  This is a stark result. The base case does NOT support the current price.
  The market is pricing in a BULL case. Let me now build the bull and bear
  cases to bracket the range.

3-4. Bull Case (WACC = 9.5%, Terminal Growth = 4.5%):
  Revenue: 2026 $499B, 2027 $599B (+20%), 2028 $719B (+20%), 2029 $835B
  (+16%), 2030 $941B (+12.7%) [Assumption - Cloud sustains 50%+ growth,
  Search 15%, YouTube 12%]
  Op Margin: 2026 34%, 2027 36%, 2028 37%, 2029 38%, 2030 38% [Assumption]
  NOPAT: 2026 $146.7B, 2027 $184.8B, 2028 $230.4B, 2029 $275.6B, 2030 $312.1B
  D&A: 2026 $45B, 2027 $75B, 2028 $105B, 2029 $125B, 2030 $140B [Assumption]
  Capex: 2026 $200B, 2027 $230B, 2028 $200B, 2029 $170B, 2030 $150B
